f: What is the definition of taṣrīf (علم التصريف) linguistically?
b: Taṣrīf linguistically means change or alteration (التغيير).

f: What is the technical definition of taṣrīf according to the ṣarf scholars?
b: It is transforming one original form into different forms for intended meanings that cannot be obtained except through those transformations.

f: How is the verb (الفعل) divided according to the number of its original letters?
b: A verb is either triliteral (ثلاثي) or quadriliteral (رباعي).

f: How is each triliteral and quadriliteral verb divided according to whether it contains additional letters?
b: Each is either mujarrad (مجرد) or mazīd fīhi (مزيد فيه).

f: How is each mujarrad or mazīd verb divided according to the condition of its letters?
b: Each is either sālim (سالم) or non-sālim (غير سالم).

f: What do the ṣarf scholars mean by a “sound” (سالم) verb?
b: A sound verb is one whose original letters corresponding to fāʾ, ʿayn, and lām are free from weak letters (حروف العلة), hamzah (الهمزة), and doubling (التضعيف).

f: What are the first and second patterns of the triliteral mujarrad verb?
b: If the past tense is فَعَلَ with fatḥah on the ʿayn, its present tense is either يَفْعُلُ or يَفْعِلُ; examples are نَصَرَ يَنْصُرُ and ضَرَبَ يَضْرِبُ.

f: What is the third pattern of the triliteral mujarrad verb?
b: If the past tense is فَعَلَ with fatḥah on the ʿayn, its present tense may be يَفْعَلُ with fatḥah on the ʿayn; examples include سَأَلَ يَسْأَلُ and مَنَعَ يَمْنَعُ.

f: What is an example of a verb that is anomalous in the third pattern?
b: أَبَى يَأْبَى is anomalous (شاذ).

f: What is the fourth pattern of the triliteral mujarrad verb?
b: If the past tense is فَعِلَ with kasrah on the ʿayn, its present tense is generally يَفْعَلُ with fatḥah on the ʿayn; an example is عَلِمَ يَعْلَمُ.

f: What is an exception to the general rule of the fourth pattern?
b: حَسِبَ يَحْسِبُ and its counterparts are exceptions.

f: What is the fifth pattern of the triliteral mujarrad verb?
b: If the past tense is فَعُلَ with ḍammah on the ʿayn, its present tense is يَفْعُلُ with ḍammah on the ʿayn; an example is حَسُنَ يَحْسُنُ.

f: What is the pattern of the quadriliteral mujarrad verb?
b: Its pattern is فَعْلَلَ.

f: What is an example of a quadriliteral mujarrad verb?
b: دَحْرَجَ, with verbal nouns دَحْرَجَةً and دِحْرَاجًا.

f: How many main categories of triliteral augmented verbs (الثلاثي المزيد فيه) are there?
b: Three: those whose past tense has four, five, or six letters.

f: What are the three four-letter patterns of the triliteral augmented verb?
b: أَفْعَلَ، فَعَّلَ، فَاعَلَ.

f: What is an example of the أَفْعَلَ pattern?
b: أَكْرَمَ — إِكْرَامًا.

f: What is an example of the فَعَّلَ pattern?
b: فَرَّحَ — تَفْرِيحًا.

f: What is an example of the فَاعَلَ pattern?
b: قَاتَلَ — مُقَاتَلَةً وقِتَالًا.

f: What are the five-letter triliteral augmented patterns beginning with tāʾ?
b: تَفَعَّلَ and تَفَاعَلَ.

f: What is an example of the تَفَعَّلَ pattern?
b: تَكَسَّرَ — تَكَسُّرًا.

f: What is an example of the تَفَاعَلَ pattern?
b: تَبَاعَدَ — تَبَاعُدًا.

f: What is the five-letter triliteral augmented pattern beginning with hamzah?
b: اِنْفَعَلَ.

f: What is an example of the اِنْفَعَلَ pattern?
b: اِنْقَطَعَ — اِنْقِطَاعًا.

f: What are the six-letter triliteral augmented patterns mentioned?
b: اِسْتَفْعَلَ، اِفْعَالَّ، اِفْعَوْعَلَ، اِفْعَوَّلَ، اِفْعَنْلَلَ، اِفْعَنْلَى.

f: What is an example of the اِسْتَفْعَلَ pattern?
b: اِسْتَخْرَجَ — اِسْتِخْرَاجًا.

f: What is an example of the اِفْعَالَّ pattern?
b: اِحْمَارَّ — اِحْمِيرَارًا.

f: What is an example of the اِفْعَوْعَلَ pattern?
b: اِعْشَوْشَبَ — اِعْشِيشَابًا.

f: What is an example of the اِفْعَوَّلَ pattern?
b: اِجْلَوَّذَ — اِجْلِوَاذًا.

f: What is an example of the اِفْعَنْلَلَ pattern?
b: اِقْعَنْسَسَ — اِقْعِنْسَاسًا.

f: What is an example of the اِفْعَنْلَى pattern?
b: اِسْلَنْقَى — اِسْلِنْقَاءً.

f: How many patterns of quadriliteral augmented verbs are mentioned?
b: Three patterns.

f: What are the three patterns of quadriliteral augmented verbs?
b: تَفَعْلَلَ، اِفْعَنْلَلَ، اِفْعَلَّلَ.

f: What is an example of the تَفَعْلَلَ pattern?
b: تَدَحْرَجَ — تَدَحْرُجًا.

f: What is an example of the اِفْعَنْلَلَ pattern?
b: اِحْرَنْجَمَ — اِحْرِنْجَامًا.

f: What is an example of the اِفْعَلَّلَ pattern?
b: اِقْشَعَرَّ — اِقْشِعْرَارًا.

f: How is the verb divided according to whether it takes an object?
b: The verb is either transitive (متعدٍّ) or intransitive (لازم).

f: What is the definition of the past-tense verb (الفعل الماضي) in Arabic grammar?
b: It is a verb that indicates a meaning that occurred in past time.

f: How is the past-tense verb built when it is active (مبني للفاعل)?
b: The active past-tense verb is built with its first letter vowelled with fatḥah, or with the first vowelled letter having fatḥah.

f: What are examples of the active past tense of نَصَرَ with its different pronouns?
b: نَصَرَ، نَصَرَا، نَصَرُوا، نَصَرْتَ، نَصَرْتُمَا، نَصَرْتُمْ، نَصَرْتِ، نَصَرْتُمَا، نَصَرْتُنَّ، نَصَرْتُ، نَصَرْنَا.

f: Does the rule for the active past tense apply only to the pattern فَعَلَ?
b: No. The same principle applies to other patterns, including أَفْعَلَ، فَعَّلَ، فَاعَلَ، فَعْلَلَ، تَفَعْلَلَ، اِفْتَعَلَ، اِنْفَعَلَ، اِسْتَفْعَلَ، اِفْعَلَّ، and اِفْعَوْعَلَ.

f: How are initial alifs treated when determining the vowels of an active past-tense verb?
b: The vowels of alifs at the beginning are not considered, because these alifs are additional letters that are pronounced when beginning speech but dropped in connected speech.

f: What is the definition of the passive past-tense verb (المبني للمفعول)?
b: It is a verb in which the doer (فاعل) is not named or specified.

f: How is the passive past-tense verb generally recognized when its first letter is vowelled?
b: Its first letter is vowelled with ḍammah.

f: What are examples of passive past-tense patterns whose first letter is vowelled with ḍammah?
b: Examples include فُعِلَ، فُعْلِلَ، أُفْعِلَ، فُعِّلَ، فُوعِلَ، and تُفُعِّلَ.

f: How is the passive past tense recognized in patterns beginning with an initial additional alif?
b: The first vowelled letter after the initial alif is vowelled with ḍammah, as in اِفْتُعِلَ and اِسْتُفْعِلَ.

f: What is the definition of the present-tense verb (الفعل المضارع) in Arabic grammar?
b: It is a verb that begins with one of the four present-tense prefixes: hamzah, nūn, tāʾ, or yāʾ.

f: What are the four present-tense prefixes (حروف المضارعة)?
b: They are الهمزة (أ)، النون (ن)، التاء (ت)، and الياء (ي), commonly remembered by the expression أَنَيْتُ or نَأْتِي.

f: What does the hamzah prefix (أ) indicate in the present tense?
b: It indicates the first-person singular, i.e. the speaker alone: أَفْعَلُ.

f: What does the nūn prefix (ن) indicate in the present tense?
b: It indicates the first person when the speaker is accompanied by another: نَفْعَلُ.

f: What does the tāʾ prefix (ت) indicate in the present tense?
b: It is used for the second person, whether singular, dual, or plural, masculine or feminine; and for the third-person feminine singular and dual.

f: What does the yāʾ prefix (ي) indicate in the present tense?
b: It is used for the third-person masculine, whether singular, dual, or plural, and for the third-person feminine plural.

f: Which persons can be represented by the present-tense prefix تـ?
b: تـ can represent the second-person singular, dual, and plural, masculine or feminine; and the third-person feminine singular and dual.

f: Which persons can be represented by the present-tense prefix يـ?
b: يـ represents the third-person masculine singular, dual, and plural, as well as the third-person feminine plural.

f: What time can the Arabic present-tense verb (الفعل المضارع) indicate?
b: It can indicate either the present or the future.

f: How does the meaning of يَفْعَلُ differ between present and future contexts?
b: يَفْعَلُ الآن indicates that the action is occurring now and is called حالًا or حاضرًا, while يَفْعَلُ غدًا indicates future time.

f: What happens to the meaning of a present-tense verb when سـ is prefixed to it?
b: It becomes restricted to future time; for example, سَيَفْعَلُ means “he will do.”

f: What happens to the meaning of a present-tense verb when سَوْفَ is prefixed to it?
b: It becomes restricted to future time; for example, سَوْفَ يَفْعَلُ means “he will do.”

f: How is the active present-tense verb (المضارع المبني للفاعل) generally recognized?
b: Its present-tense prefix (حرف المضارعة) is generally vowelled with fatḥah.

f: What is the exception to the fatḥah rule for the present-tense prefix of an active verb?
b: If the past-tense verb has four letters, its present-tense prefix is always vowelled with ḍammah.

f: What are examples of four-letter past-tense verbs whose active present-tense prefixes have ḍammah?
b: يُدَحْرِجُ، يُكْرِمُ، يُقَاتِلُ، and يُفَرِّحُ.

f: What is the sign of the active present tense for a verb whose past tense has four letters?
b: The letter immediately before the final letter of the present tense is always vowelled with kasrah.

f: What are examples of active present-tense verbs across the various triliteral and augmented patterns?
b: Examples include يَضْرِبُ، يَعْلَمُ، يُدَحْرِجُ، يُكْرِمُ، يُقَاتِلُ، يُفَرِّحُ، يَتَكَسَّرُ، يَتَبَاعَدُ، يَنْقَطِعُ، يَجْتَمِعُ، يَحْمَرُّ، يَحْمَارُّ، يَسْتَخْرِجُ، يَعْشَوْشِبُ، يَقْعَنْسِسُ، يَسْلَنْقِي، يَجْلَوَّذُ، يَتَدَحْرَجُ، يَحْرَنْجِمُ، and يَقْشَعِرُّ.

f: How is the passive present-tense verb (المضارع المبني للمفعول) formed?
b: Its present-tense prefix is vowelled with ḍammah, and the letter before its final letter is vowelled with fatḥah.

f: What are examples of passive present-tense verbs?
b: يُنْصَرُ، يُدَحْرَجُ، يُكْرَمُ، يُقَاتَلُ، يُفَرَّحُ، and يُسْتَخْرَجُ.

f: What happens when the negative particles مَا and لَا enter upon the Arabic present-tense verb?
b: They do not change the form of the present-tense verb.

f: What are examples of مَا and لَا negating a present-tense verb?
b: لَا يَنْصُرُ and مَا يَنْصُرُ; the same form remains with the dual and plural, such as مَا يَنْصُرَانِ and مَا يَنْصُرُونَ.

f: What happens when a jussive particle (جازم) enters upon the Arabic present-tense verb?
b: It removes the final vowel of the singular form and removes the nūn of the dual, masculine plural, and second-person feminine singular forms.

f: Which nūn is not removed by a jussive particle?
b: The nūn of the third-person feminine plural is not removed because it is a pronoun, like the wāw of the masculine plural.

f: What are examples of the jussive particle لَمْ with نَصَرَ in the different forms?
b: لَمْ يَنْصُرْ، لَمْ يَنْصُرَا، لَمْ يَنْصُرُوا، لَمْ تَنْصُرْ، لَمْ تَنْصُرَا، لَمْ يَنْصُرْنَ، لَمْ تَنْصُرْ، لَمْ تَنْصُرَا، لَمْ تَنْصُرُوا، لَمْ تَنْصُرِي، لَمْ تَنْصُرَا، لَمْ تَنْصُرْنَ، لَمْ أَنْصُرْ، and لَمْ نَنْصُرْ.

f: What happens when a subjunctive/accusative particle (ناصب) enters upon the Arabic present-tense verb?
b: The final ḍammah is changed to fatḥah, and the nūns of the dual, masculine plural, and second-person feminine singular are dropped.

f: Which nūn is not dropped when a subjunctive/accusative particle enters upon the present tense?
b: The nūn of the third-person feminine plural is not dropped because it is a pronoun.

f: What are examples of the subjunctive particle لَنْ with نَصَرَ?
b: لَنْ يَنْصُرَ، لَنْ يَنْصُرَا، لَنْ يَنْصُرُوا، and similarly the remaining forms, ending with لَنْ أَنْصُرَ and لَنْ نَنْصُرَ.

f: What is one jussive particle used to command or request an action from an absent person?
b: The imperative lām (لام الأمر), such as لِيَنْصُرْ “let him help.”

f: How is لام الأمر used with the third-person masculine singular, dual, and plural?
b: لِيَنْصُرْ، لِيَنْصُرَا، لِيَنْصُرُوا.

f: How is لام الأمر used with the third-person feminine singular, dual, and plural?
b: لِتَنْصُرْ، لِتَنْصُرَا، لِيَنْصُرْنَ.

f: What is another jussive particle used to prohibit an action?
b: The prohibitive لَا (لا الناهية).

f: How is لا الناهية used with the third-person masculine forms?
b: لا يَنْصُرْ، لا يَنْصُرَا، لا يَنْصُرُوا.

f: How is لا الناهية used with the third-person feminine forms?
b: لا تَنْصُرْ، لا تَنْصُرَا، لا يَنْصُرْنَ.

f: How is لا الناهية used to prohibit the second-person masculine singular, dual, and plural?
b: لا تَنْصُرْ، لا تَنْصُرَا، لا تَنْصُرُوا.

f: How is لا الناهية used to prohibit the second-person feminine singular, dual, and plural?
b: لا تَنْصُرِي، لا تَنْصُرَا، لا تَنْصُرْنَ.

f: How is the jussive form of تَنْصُرْنَ and similar forms treated when forming the imperative?
b: The same rule applies by analogy to all other examples.

f: What is the imperative by form (فعل الأمر بالصيغة)?
b: It is the imperative addressed to the present addressee (أمر الحاضر), formed from the jussive present-tense verb.

f: How is the imperative formed when the letter after the present-tense prefix is vowelled?
b: The present-tense prefix is removed, and the remaining form is given its jussive form.

f: How is the imperative of تَدَحْرَجَ formed when the letter after the present-tense prefix is vowelled?
b: Remove the تـ of the present tense from تَتَدَحْرَجُ and use the remaining jussive form: دَحْرِجْ، دَحْرِجَا، دَحْرِجُوا، دَحْرِجِي، دَحْرِجَا، دَحْرِجْنَ.

f: What verbs follow the same imperative-formation rule as تَدَحْرَجَ?
b: فَرَّحَ، قَاتَلَ، تَكَسَّرَ، تَبَاعَدَ، and تَدَحْرَجَ.

f: How is the imperative formed when the letter after the present-tense prefix is sākin (unvowelled)?
b: The present-tense prefix is removed, the remaining form is made jussive, and a hamzat al-waṣl (همزة الوصل) is added at the beginning, normally with kasrah.

f: When is the hamzat al-waṣl added to the beginning of an imperative with kasrah?
b: It is added with kasrah when the letter following the removed present-tense prefix is sākin, unless the ʿayn of the present tense is ḍammah.

f: When is the hamzat al-waṣl of an imperative vowelled with ḍammah instead of kasrah?
b: It is vowelled with ḍammah when the ʿayn of the present-tense verb is ḍammah.

f: What are the imperative forms of أَنْصَرَ according to the rule for a present tense beginning with a sākin after the prefix?
b: أَنْصُرْ، أَنْصُرَا، أَنْصُرُوا، أَنْصُرِي، أَنْصُرَا، أَنْصُرْنَ.

f: What are examples of imperatives formed with an initial hamzat al-waṣl because the letter after the present-tense prefix is sākin?
b: اِضْرِبْ، اِعْلَمْ، اِنْقَطِعْ، اِجْتَمِعْ، and اِسْتَخْرِجْ.

f: Why is the hamzah of أَكْرِمْ pronounced with fatḥah according to the passage?
b: The passage explains that the hamzah of أَكْرِمْ is opened based on the rejected original form, since the original form of تَكْرِمُ would have been تُؤَكْرِمُ, involving the original structure.

f: What happens when two tāʾs occur at the beginning of the present tense of تَفَعَّلَ?
b: Both tāʾs may be retained, as in تَتَجَنَّبُ. Alternatively, one of the two tāʾs may be omitted.

f: What happens when two tāʾs occur at the beginning of the present tense of تَفَاعَلَ?
b: Both tāʾs may be retained, as in تَتَقَاتَلُ, or one of them may be omitted.

f: What happens when two tāʾs occur at the beginning of the present tense of تَفَعْلَلَ?
b: Both tāʾs may be retained, as in تَتَدَحْرَجُ, or one of them may be omitted.

f: Is it permissible to omit one of two tāʾs occurring at the beginning of a present-tense verb?
b: Yes. When two tāʾs occur at the beginning of the present tense of patterns such as تَفَعَّلَ، تَفَاعَلَ، and تَفَعْلَلَ, either both may be retained or one may be omitted.

f: What Qurʾānic examples are given for omitting one of two initial tāʾs?
b: Examples include تَذَكَّرُونَ، تَطَيَّرْنَا، and نُنَزِّلُ الْمَلَائِكَةَ, as cited in the passage.

f: When is the tāʾ of the اِفْتَعَلَ pattern changed into ṭāʾ (ط)?
b: When the first root letter (فاء الكلمة) of the اِفْتَعَلَ form is ص، ض، ط، or ظ, its tāʾ is changed into ṭāʾ.

f: How is اِفْتَعَلَ formed from the root ص ل ح?
b: اِصْطَلَحَ, because the first root letter is ص, so the tāʾ of اِفْتَعَلَ changes to ط.

f: How is اِفْتَعَلَ formed from the root ض ر ب?
b: اِضْطَرَبَ, because the first root letter is ض, so the tāʾ changes to ط.

f: How is اِفْتَعَلَ formed from the root ط ر د?
b: اِطَّرَدَ, because the first root letter is ط, so the tāʾ changes to ṭāʾ and assimilation occurs.

f: How is اِفْتَعَلَ formed from the root ظ ل م?
b: اِظْطَلَمَ according to the pattern given in the passage, because the first root letter is ظ and the tāʾ changes to ṭāʾ.

f: Does the change of the tāʾ to ṭāʾ in اِفْتَعَلَ apply only to the past tense?
b: No. The change applies throughout all the derived forms of the verb.

f: What are examples of the various forms of اِصْطَلَحَ after the tāʾ of اِفْتَعَلَ changes to ṭāʾ?
b: اِصْطَلَحَ، يَصْطَلِحُ، اِصْطِلَاحًا، مُصْطَلِحٌ، مُصْطَلَحٌ عَلَيْهِ، اِصْطَلِحْ، and لَا تَصْطَلِحْ.

f: When is the tāʾ of the اِفْتَعَلَ pattern changed into dāl (د)?
b: When the first root letter (فاء الكلمة) is د، ذ، or ز, the tāʾ of اِفْتَعَلَ changes into dāl.

f: How is اِفْتَعَلَ formed from a root beginning with د?
b: The tāʾ changes into د, as in اِدَّرَأَ from دَرَأَ.

f: How is اِفْتَعَلَ formed from a root beginning with ذ?
b: The tāʾ changes into د, as in اِذَّكَرَ from ذَكَرَ.

f: How is اِفْتَعَلَ formed from a root beginning with ز?
b: The tāʾ changes into د, as in اِزْدَجَرَ from زَجَرَ.

f: What are the two types of emphatic nūn (نون التأكيد)?
b: There are two types: the light emphatic nūn (نون التأكيد الخفيفة) and the heavy emphatic nūn (نون التأكيد الثقيلة).

f: How is the nūn of feminine plural (نون جماعة النساء) treated when followed by the emphatic nūn?
b: It remains with kasrah, and an alif is inserted after the feminine-plural nūn to separate the two nūns.

f: Why is an alif inserted after the nūn of the feminine plural before the heavy emphatic nūn?
b: It separates the two consecutive nūns, as in forms such as أَذْهَبَنَّ for the dual and أَذْهَبْنَانَّ for the feminine plural, according to the passage.

f: Why is an alif not inserted before the light emphatic nūn?
b: Because doing so would result in the impermissible meeting of two sukūns (التقاء الساكنين) in this context.

f: When is the meeting of two sukūns permissible in Arabic?
b: It is permissible when the first of the two is a letter of madd and the second is a letter with sukūn, such as دَابَّةٌ.

f: What happens to the nūn of the five verbs when an emphatic nūn is attached?
b: The nūn found in the five verbs is deleted.

f: Which five present-tense forms are called the five verbs (الأمثلة الخمسة)?
b: يَفْعَلَانِ، تَفْعَلَانِ، يَفْعَلُونَ، تَفْعَلُونَ، and تَفْعَلِينَ.

f: What happens to the wāw of يَفْعَلُونَ and تَفْعَلُونَ when the emphatic nūn is attached?
b: The wāw is deleted unless the preceding letter has fatḥah.

f: What happens to the yāʾ of تَفْعَلِينَ when the emphatic nūn is attached?
b: The yāʾ is deleted unless the preceding letter has fatḥah.

f: What examples illustrate retention of the wāw or yāʾ before emphatic nūn when the preceding letter has fatḥah?
b: Examples include لَا تَخْشَوْنَ، لَا تَخْشَيْنَ، وَلَتَبْلُوَنَّ, and فَإِمَّا تَرَيِنَّ, as cited in the passage.

f: How is the final vowel of a verb determined when the heavy or light emphatic nūn (نون التوكيد) is attached?
b: With the emphatic nūns, the final vowel is fatḥah for the third-person singular masculine and feminine forms, ḍammah for the third-person masculine plural, and kasrah for the second-person feminine singular.

f: How is the emphatic imperative for an absent masculine singular formed with the heavy nūn?
b: لِيَنْصُرَنَّ.

f: How is the emphatic imperative for an absent masculine dual formed with the heavy nūn?
b: لِيَنْصُرَانِّ.

f: How is the emphatic imperative for an absent masculine plural formed with the heavy nūn?
b: لِيَنْصُرُنَّ.

f: How is the emphatic imperative for an absent feminine singular formed with the heavy nūn?
b: لِتَنْصُرَنَّ.

f: How is the emphatic imperative for an absent feminine dual formed with the heavy nūn?
b: لِتَنْصُرَانِّ.

f: How is the emphatic imperative for an absent feminine plural formed with the heavy nūn?
b: لِيَنْصُرْنَانِّ.

f: How is the imperative for an absent person emphasized with the light nūn?
b: The forms are: لِيَنْصُرَنْ، لِيَنْصُرَا، لِتَنْصُرَنْ.

f: How is the emphatic imperative for the second-person masculine singular formed with the heavy nūn?
b: اُنْصُرَنَّ.

f: How is the emphatic imperative for the second-person masculine dual formed with the heavy nūn?
b: اُنْصُرَانِّ.

f: How is the emphatic imperative for the second-person masculine plural formed with the heavy nūn?
b: اُنْصُرُنَّ.

f: How is the emphatic imperative for the second-person feminine singular formed with the heavy nūn?
b: اُنْصُرِنَّ.

f: How is the emphatic imperative for the second-person feminine dual formed with the heavy nūn?
b: اُنْصُرَانِّ.

f: How is the emphatic imperative for the second-person feminine plural formed with the heavy nūn?
b: اُنْصُرْنَانِّ.

f: How are the second-person imperative forms emphasized with the light nūn?
b: The forms are: اُنْصُرَنْ، اُنْصُرَا، اُنْصُرَنْ.

f: What is the general rule for forming the active participle (اسم الفاعل) from a triliteral verb?
b: It is generally formed on the pattern فَاعِلٌ, such as نَاصِرٌ from نَصَرَ.

f: What is the general rule for forming the passive participle (اسم المفعول) from a triliteral verb?
b: It is generally formed on the pattern مَفْعُولٌ, such as مَنْصُورٌ from نَصَرَ.

f: How are the pronouns of the active and passive participles declined?
b: They are made singular, dual, and plural, and masculine and feminine, according to the pronoun or noun they describe.

f: What does the passage indicate about the forms مَمْرُورٌ بِهِ and similar passive participles?
b: The active and passive participles can take the appropriate attached pronouns according to the construction, such as مَمْرُورٌ بِهِ، مَمْرُورٌ بِكُمْ، مَمْرُورٌ بِي، and مَمْرُورٌ بِنَا.

f: Can the pattern فَعِيلٌ function as an active participle?
b: Yes. فَعِيلٌ can sometimes have the meaning of the active participle, such as الرَّحِيم meaning الرَّاحِم.

f: Can the pattern فَعِيلٌ function as a passive participle?
b: Yes. فَعِيلٌ can sometimes have the meaning of the passive participle, such as القَتِيل meaning المَقْتُول.

f: How is the active participle formed from a verb with more than three original letters?
b: Replace the present-tense prefix with a mīm bearing ḍammah and put kasrah on the letter before the final letter.

f: How is the passive participle formed from a verb with more than three original letters?
b: Replace the present-tense prefix with a mīm bearing ḍammah and put fatḥah on the letter before the final letter.

f: What is the active participle of أَكْرَمَ?
b: مُكْرِمٌ.

f: What is the passive participle of أَكْرَمَ?
b: مُكْرَمٌ.

f: What is the active participle of دَحْرَجَ?
b: مُدَحْرِجٌ.

f: What is the passive participle of دَحْرَجَ?
b: مُدَحْرَجٌ.

f: What is the active participle of اِسْتَخْرَجَ?
b: مُسْتَخْرِجٌ.

f: What is the passive participle of اِسْتَخْرَجَ?
b: مُسْتَخْرَجٌ.

f: Can the active and passive participles have the same outward form?
b: Yes. In some cases the active and passive participles are identical in form, and the intended meaning is determined by context.

f: What are examples where the active and passive participles have the same outward form?
b: مُحَابٌّ، مُتَحَابٌّ، مُخْتَارٌ، مُضْطَرٌّ، مُغْتَدٍ، مُنْصَبٌّ، مُنْجَابٌ, and similar forms.

f: What is a doubled verb (الفعل المضاعف)?
b: A doubled verb is a verb in which two of its original letters are of the same type, producing a doubled consonant.

f: What is a doubled triliteral verb?
b: In a triliteral verb, it is a verb whose ʿayn and lām radicals are identical, such as رَدَّ.

f: What is the underlying original form of رَدَّ?
b: Its original form is رَدَدَ.

f: What is the underlying original form of أَعَدَّ?
b: Its original form is أَعْدَدَ.

f: What is a doubled quadriliteral verb?
b: It is a quadriliteral verb whose first and second root positions are of the same type, and whose third and fourth root positions are also of the same type.

f: What is another name for a doubled quadriliteral verb?
b: It is also called المُطَابِق.

f: What is an example of a doubled quadriliteral verb?
b: زَلْزَلَ, whose verbal nouns include زَلْزَلَةً and زِلْزَالًا.

f: Why are doubled verbs discussed together with defective verbs (المعتلات)?
b: Because the consonant affected by doubling can undergo processes such as substitution (الإبدال) and deletion (الحذف), similar to what occurs in defective verbs.

f: What is an example of substitution involving a doubled verb?
b: أَمْلَيْتُ may be used in the sense of أَمْلَلْتُ, involving substitution of the doubled consonant.

f: What are examples of deletion involving doubled verbs?
b: قِسْتُ and ظِلْتُ can occur from قَسَسْتُ and ظَلَلْتُ, and أَحْسَسْتُ can become أَحْسَتْ, according to the examples given.

f: What is idghām (الإدغام) in a doubled verb?
b: It is making the first of two identical consonants sākin and merging it into the second, so the first is called المُدْغَم and the second المُدْغَم فيه.

f: When is idghām obligatory in a doubled verb?
b: It is obligatory in forms such as مَدَّ يَمُدُّ and أَعَدَّ يُعِدُّ, and in similar forms.

f: Is idghām obligatory in the verbal noun of a doubled verb?
b: Yes, as in مَدٌّ as the verbal noun of مَدَّ.

f: What happens to a doubled verb when an alif of the pronoun is attached?
b: Idghām occurs, as in مَدَّا.

f: What happens to a doubled verb when the wāw of the pronoun is attached?
b: Idghām occurs, as in مَدُّوا.

f: What happens to a doubled verb when the yāʾ of the pronoun is attached?
b: Idghām occurs, as in مَدِّي.

f: When is idghām prohibited in a doubled verb?
b: It is prohibited when the doubled verb is followed by a suffix beginning with a vowelled consonant that prevents the two identical consonants from being merged, such as مَدَدْتُ، مَدَدْنَا، مَدَدْتَ، مَدَدْتُنَّ، مَدَدْنَ، يَمْدُدْنَ، تَمْدُدْنَ، أَمْدُدْنَ، and لَا تَمْدُدْنَ.

f: When is idghām optional in a doubled verb?
b: It is optional when a jussive particle enters upon the third-person singular form of a doubled verb.

f: How can a doubled verb whose present-tense ʿayn is kasrah appear after a jussive particle?
b: It may undergo idghām, producing forms such as لَمْ يَفِرْ, or the doubling may be separated, as in لَمْ يَفْرِرْ.

f: How can a doubled verb whose present-tense ʿayn is fatḥah appear after a jussive particle?
b: It may undergo idghām, producing لَمْ يَعَضْ, or the doubling may be separated, as in لَمْ يَعْضَضْ.

f: Which other doubled verbs follow the same jussive rule as يَفِرُّ and يَعَضُّ?
b: Verbs such as يَقْشَعِرُّ، يَحْمَرُّ, and يَحْمَارُّ follow the same general principle.

f: What happens when the ʿayn of a doubled verb's present tense is ḍammah and it is made jussive?
b: Three possibilities are permitted: the three vowel movements may occur with idghām, or the doubling may be separated (فك الإدغام).

f: How does the verb مَدَّ appear in the jussive when its present tense has a ḍammah on the ʿayn?
b: It can appear with the three possible vowels on the dāl while retaining idghām, or with the doubling separated: لَمْ يَمُدْ

f: Does the same rule of optional idghām apply to the imperative of doubled verbs?
b: Yes. The same principle applies to the imperative.

f: What are examples of the imperative of doubled verbs with optional idghām?
b: فِرْ and عَضَّ may be used with idghām, while اِفْرِرْ and أَعْضِضْ show the doubled consonants separated.

f: How can the imperative of مَدَّ be formed when idghām is optional?
b: It may retain idghām with the possible vowelings of the dāl, or have the doubling separated as أُمْدُدْ.

f: What is the active participle of مَدَّ?
b: مَادٌّ.

f: How can the active participle of مَدَّ be declined for the dual?
b: مَادَّانِ.

f: What form of the active participle of مَدَّ is mentioned for the plural?
b: مَادُّونَ.

f: What is an al-muʿtall (المعتل) verb in Arabic morphology?
b: It is a verb in which one of its original root letters is a ḥarf ʿillah (حرف علة): و، ا، ي. These are called the letters of madd and līn (حروف المد واللين). The alif in a weak verb is always originally derived from either و or ي.

f: What are the seven types of al-muʿtall (المعتل) verbs?
b: They are classified according to the position and type of the weak letter. The first is al-muʿtall al-fāʾ (المعتل الفاء), called al-mithāl (المثال); the second is al-muʿtall al-ʿayn (المعتل العين), called al-ajwaf (الأجوف); the remaining types concern weakness in the final radical and combinations of weak radicals.

f: Why is a verb with a weak first radical called al-mithāl (المثال)?
b: It is called al-mithāl because its weak first radical resembles the treatment of a sound verb in its ability to accept the various vowel endings in many forms.

f: What happens to an initial wāw in the present tense of a mithāl verb when the present form is يَفْعِلُ?
b: The wāw is deleted from the present tense when the verb is on the pattern يَفْعِلُ, with kasrah on the ʿayn. For example: وَعَدَ → يَعِدُ.

f: What happens to the initial wāw of a mithāl verb in its verbal noun on the pattern فِعْلَة?
b: The wāw is deleted, as in وَعَدَ → عِدَة.

f: What forms of وَعَدَ illustrate the deletion and preservation of its initial wāw?
b: وَعَدَ، يَعِدُ، عِدَةً، وَعْدًا، وَاعِدٌ، مَوْعُودٌ، عِدْ، لَا تَعِدْ. The wāw is deleted in يَعِدُ، عِدَةً، عِدْ but remains in forms such as وَعْدٌ، وَاعِدٌ، مَوْعُودٌ.

f: When can the deleted initial wāw of a mithāl verb return?
b: If the kasrah that caused its deletion is removed, the deleted wāw returns. For example, وَعَدَ → يَعِدُ, but after a jussive environment in which the relevant vowel is removed, one may have لَمْ يُوعَدْ.

f: How does an initial wāw behave in the present tense pattern يَفْعَلُ?
b: It remains, as in وَجِلَ → يَوْجَلُ. However, when the wāw becomes sākin and the preceding letter is kasrah, it changes into yāʾ because of the combination of sukūn and kasrah.

f: What happens to the initial wāw in وَجِلَ → يَوْجَلُ when the preceding vowel is kasrah?
b: The wāw changes into yāʾ because the wāw is sākin while the preceding letter has kasrah. If the preceding vowel is ḍammah, the wāw remains wāw.

f: What happens to the initial wāw in the present tense pattern يَفْعُلُ?
b: It remains unchanged. For example: وَجُهَ → يَوْجُهُ; in the imperative: أَوْجُهْ and in the prohibition: لَا تَوْجُهْ.

f: Why is the wāw omitted from يَذَرُ and يَدَعُ treated differently?
b: The wāw is omitted from يَذَرُ because it is treated as equivalent in meaning to يَدَعُ. The past forms of يَدَعُ and يَذَرُ have also fallen out of normal usage. The deletion of the first radical is evidence that it was originally a wāw.

f: How does an initial yāʾ behave in a mithāl verb?
b: Unlike an initial wāw, the initial yāʾ remains in all cases. Examples include يَمَنَ → يَيْمَنُ, يَسَرَ → يَيْسَرُ, and يَئِسَ → يَيْأَسُ.

f: What happens to the initial yāʾ in the afʿala form of a yāʾ-initial verb?
b: In the أفعل form, the yāʾ may be changed into wāw when it becomes sākin and the preceding vowel is ḍammah. For example: أَيْسَرَ → يُوسِرُ, giving مُوسِرٌ.

f: Why is the yāʾ changed into wāw in forms such as يُوسِرُ?
b: Because the yāʾ is sākin and the preceding letter has ḍammah, so the yāʾ is changed into a wāw.

f: What happens to a yāʾ-initial verb in the iftaʿala (افتعل) form?
b: Examples include اِتَّعَدَ / يَتَّعِدُ and اِتَّسَرَ

f: What is the morphological treatment of وَدَّ and similar doubled weak verbs?
b: Its treatment follows that of عَضَّ

f: What is al-muʿtall al-ʿayn (المعتل العين) called, and why?
b: It is called al-ajwaf (الأجوف) because its middle radical is weak. It is also called ذو الثلاثة because its past tense is generally three letters in its basic form. Examples are قَالَ and بَاعَ.

f: What happens to the middle weak radical of a basic triliteral hollow verb in the past tense?
b: The middle radical is changed into alif when it is originally either wāw or yāʾ, because the weak letter is moving and the preceding letter is fatḥah. Examples: صَانَ and بَاعَ.

f: What happens to a hollow verb when it is connected to the pronouns of the speaker, addressee, or plural?
b: The original weak radical reappears because the conditions for changing it into alif no longer apply. For example: قُلْتُ، قُلْتَ، قُلْتُمْ، قُلْتُنَّ، قُلْنَا and بِعْتُ، بِعْتَ، بِعْتُمْ، بِعْتُنَّ، بِعْنَا.

f: How is a hollow verb pronounced when it is made passive in the past tense?
b: The first radical is given kasrah, and the weak middle radical undergoes the necessary naql (النقل) and qalb (القلب). Thus صَانَ → صِينَ and بَاعَ → بِيعَ.

f: What happens to a hollow verb in the present tense?
b: The weak middle radical undergoes naql, and, where required, qalb. Examples are يَصُونُ، يَبِيعُ، يَخَافُ، يَهَابُ.

f: What happens when a jussive particle such as لَمْ enters upon a hollow present-tense verb?
b: The middle weak radical is deleted if the letter following it is sākin, but it remains if the following letter is moving.

f: How does لَمْ affect the hollow verb يَصُونُ in the various pronoun forms?
b: Examples include: لَمْ يَصُنْ، لَمْ يَصُونَا، لَمْ يَصُونُوا، لَمْ تَصُنْ، لَمْ تَصُونَا، لَمْ يَصُنْ، لَمْ تَصُنْ، لَمْ تَصُونَا، لَمْ تَصُونُوا، لَمْ تَصُونِي، لَمْ تَصُونَا، لَمْ يَصُنْ، لَمْ أَصُنْ، لَمْ نَصُنْ.

f: How does the jussive affect the hollow verbs يَبِيعُ and يَخَافُ?
b: They follow the same rule: لَمْ يَبِعْ، لَمْ يَبِيعَا and لَمْ يَخَفْ، لَمْ يَخَافَا. The middle weak letter is deleted when the following letter is sākin and retained when the following letter is moving.

f: How is the imperative formed from the hollow verb صَانَ
b: It follows the jussive form: صُنْ، صُومَا، صُومُوا، صُونِي، صُومَا، صُنْ.

f: What happens when nūn al-tawkīd (نون التأكيد) is attached to a hollow verb?
b: The weak middle radical may be retained or undergo deletion according to the surrounding letters and vowels. The source gives examples such as صُونَنَّ، صُونَانِّ، صُنَّ and corresponding forms of بَاعَ and خَافَ.

f: How many patterns of augmented triliteral hollow verbs are mentioned in the passage?
b: Four patterns are mentioned: أَجَابَ، اِسْتَقَامَ، اِنْقَادَ، اِخْتَارَ.

f: What are examples of the four augmented triliteral hollow verb patterns mentioned in the passage?
b: أَجَابَ → يُجِيبُ → إِجَابَةً؛ اِسْتَقَامَ → يَسْتَقِيمُ → اِسْتِقَامَةً؛ اِنْقَادَ → يَنْقَادُ → اِنْقِيَادًا؛ اِخْتَارَ → يَخْتَارُ → اِخْتِيَارًا.

f: How are the augmented triliteral hollow verbs made passive?
b: Their passive forms undergo the corresponding changes in the weak radical: أُجِيبَ / يُجَابُ، اُسْتُقِيمَ / يُسْتَقَامُ، اُنْقِيدَ / يُنْقَادُ، اُخْتِيرَ

f: What are the imperative forms of the four augmented triliteral hollow verbs mentioned in the passage?
b: أَجِبْ، أَجِيبَا؛ اِسْتَقِمْ، اِسْتَقِيمَا؛ اِنْقَدْ، اِنْقَادَا؛ اِخْتَرْ، اِخْتَارَا.

f: What kinds of hollow verbs can retain their weak letter in augmented forms without the same deletion occurring?
b: Forms such as قَوَّلَ / قَاوَلَ، تَقَوَّلَ / تَقَاوَلَ، زَيَّنَ / تَزَيَّنَ، سَايَرَ / تَسَايَرَ، أَسْوَدَ / اِسْوَدَّ، اِبْيَضَّ

f: How is the active participle (اسم الفاعل) formed from a hollow triliteral verb?
b: In a basic triliteral hollow verb, the middle weak letter is treated according to its origin. If it is originally wāw, it appears as a hamzah in the active participle, as in صَانَ → صَائِنٌ. If it is originally yāʾ, it likewise appears as a hamzah, as in بَاعَ → بَائِعٌ.

f: What happens to the weak middle radical when forming the active participle of a hollow verb?
b: The weak radical is changed into hamzah in the active participle of the basic triliteral hollow verb, e.g. صَائِنٌ and بَائِعٌ.

f: How is the active participle of an augmented hollow verb formed?
b: It undergoes the corresponding qalb (القلب) of the weak radical, following the morphological changes of the verb. Examples include مُجِيبٌ، مُسْتَقِيمٌ، مُنْقَادٌ، مُخْتَارٌ.

f: How is the passive participle of an augmented hollow verb formed?
b: It follows the same weak-letter treatment as the present tense (المضارع) of the verb. Examples include مُجَابٌ، مُسْتَقَامٌ، مُنْقَادٌ، مُخْتَارٌ.

f: What is al-muʿtall al-lām (المعتل اللام) called?
b: It is called al-nāqiṣ (الناقص) because its final root letter is weak. It is also called dhū al-arbaʿah (ذو الأربعة) because its past tense was traditionally described in this classification as having four letters when certain forms are considered.

f: What happens to the final wāw or yāʾ of a basic triliteral defective verb in the past tense?
b: The final wāw or yāʾ becomes alif when it is moving and the preceding letter has fatḥah. Examples are غَزَا، رَمَى، عَصَا، رَحَى.

f: What happens to the final weak radical in augmented verbs and their passive participles?
b: The same change to alif occurs when the conditions for the change are present. Examples include أَعْطَى، اشْتَرَى، اسْتَقْصَى and their passive participles مُعْطًى، مُشْتَرًى، مُسْتَقْصًى.

f: Does the final weak radical remain visible when the defective verb is made passive in the present tense?
b: The final weak radical may appear as an alif in the passive present form according to the morphological pattern, as in يُغْزَى.

f: What happens to the final weak radical of a defective verb in the past tense when attached to the plural masculine pronoun واو الجماعة?
b: The final weak radical is always deleted before واو الجماعة. For example: غَزَا → غَزَوْا, رَمَى → رَمَوْا, رَضِيَ → رَضُوا, and سَرُوَ → سَرُوا.

f: When is the final weak radical deleted from a defective past verb in forms such as فعلتُ and فعلتا?
b: In forms such as فَعَلْتَ، فَعَلْتُ، فَعَلْتَا, the final weak radical is deleted when the letter before it has fatḥah. Otherwise, it remains according to the relevant conjugation.

f: What are the principal past-tense forms of غَزَا illustrating deletion of the final weak radical?
b: غَزَا، غَزَوْا، غَزَتْ، غَزَتَا، غَزَوْنَ، غَزَوْتَ، غَزَوْتُمَا، غَزَوْتُمْ، غَزَوْتُنَّ، غَزَوْتُ، غَزَوْنَا.

f: What are the principal past-tense forms of رَمَى illustrating treatment of the final yāʾ?
b: رَمَى، رَمَوْا، رَمَتْ، رَمَتَا، رَمَيْنَ، رَمَيْتَ، رَمَيْتُمَا، رَمَيْتُمْ، رَمَيْتُنَّ، رَمَيْتُ، رَمَيْنَا.

f: What are the principal past-tense forms of رَضِيَ illustrating treatment of the final yāʾ?
b: رَضِيَ، رَضُوا، رَضِيَتْ، رَضِيَتَا، رَضِينَ، رَضِيتَ، رَضِيتُمَا، رَضِيتُمْ، رَضِيتُنَّ، رَضِيتُ، رَضِينَا.

f: What are the principal past-tense forms of a defective verb such as سَرُوَ when its final radical is wāw?
b: سَرُوَ، سَرُوا، سَرُوَتْ، سَرُوَتَا، سَرُونَ، سَرُوْتَ، سَرُوْتُمَا، سَرُوْتُمْ، سَرُوْتُنَّ، سَرُوْتُ، سَرُوْنَا.

f: Why is the vowel before واو الجماعة different in forms such as غَزَوْا، رَمَوْا، رَضُوا، سَرُوا?
b: When واو الجماعة attaches to a defective verb after deletion of the final radical, the vowel before the wāw is preserved as fatḥah if that is the preceding vowel, while ḍammah is used when the preceding vowel was ḍammah or kasrah.

f: What is the original form of رَضُوا, and what morphological change produces its final form?
b: Its underlying form is رَضِيُوا. The movement of the yāʾ is transferred to the preceding ḍād, producing رَضُوا after the necessary deletion and contraction.

f: What happens to the final radical of a defective verb in the present tense?
b: In the indicative (الرفع), the final weak radical is sākin in the relevant form; in the jussive (الجزم) it is deleted; in the subjunctive (النصب) the final wāw or yāʾ is given fatḥah, while the alif remains unchanged.

f: What happens to the nūns of the five verbs when a jussive or subjunctive particle enters upon a defective verb?
b: The nūns of the five verbs (الأفعال الخمسة) are deleted, except for the nūn of the feminine plural.

f: What happens to يَغْزُو and its dual and masculine plural forms under the jussive?
b: The forms are لَمْ يَغْزُ، لَمْ يَغْزُوَا، لَمْ يَغْزُوا. The final weak radical is deleted in the singular, while the dual and masculine plural retain the relevant form with the nūn removed.

f: What happens to يَرْمِي and its dual and masculine plural forms under the jussive?
b: The forms are لَمْ يَرْمِ، لَمْ يَرْمِيَا، لَمْ يَرْمُوا.

f: What happens to يَرْضَى under the jussive and subjunctive?
b: Under the jussive: لَمْ يَرْضَ. Under the subjunctive, the alif remains: لَنْ يَرْضَى.

f: How does the defective verb behave in the dual and feminine plural forms of the present tense?
b: The final weak radical is retained in the dual and feminine plural forms. It is deleted in the masculine plural and in the second-person feminine singular where the grammatical structure requires it.

f: What are the present-tense forms of غَزَا → يَغْزُو?
b: يَغْزُو، يَغْزُوَانِ، يَغْزُونَ؛ تَغْزُو، تَغْزُوَانِ، يَغْزُونَ؛ تَغْزُو، تَغْزُوَانِ، تَغْزُونَ؛ تَغْزِينَ، تَغْزُوَانِ، تَغْزُونَ؛ أَغْزُو، نَغْزُو.

f: What are the present-tense forms of رَمَى → يَرْمِي?
b: يَرْمِي، يَرْمِيَانِ، يَرْمُونَ؛ تَرْمِي، تَرْمِيَانِ، يَرْمِينَ؛ تَرْمِي، تَرْمِيَانِ، تَرْمُونَ؛ تَرْمِينَ، تَرْمِيَانِ، تَرْمِينَ؛ أَرْمِي، نَرْمِي.

f: What is the underlying form of يَرْمُونَ, and how is its final form produced?
b: Its underlying form is يَرْمِيُونَ. It undergoes the same morphological treatment as رَضِيُوا → رَضُوا, resulting in يَرْمُونَ.

f: How are defective verbs whose preceding letter has kasrah treated in the present tense?
b: They follow the same pattern as يَرْمِي. Examples include يَهْدِي، يُنَاجِي، يَرْتَجِي، يَنْبَرِي، يَسْتَدْعِي، يَرْعَوِي.

f: How are defective verbs whose preceding letter has fatḥah treated in the present tense?
b: They follow the same general rules of defective verbs. Examples include يَتَمَطَّى، يَتَصَابَى، يَتَقَلْسَى.

f: How is the second-person feminine singular distinguished from the feminine plural in defective verbs such as تَرْمِي and تَرْمِينَ?
b: Their pronunciation may coincide in certain forms, but their underlying grammatical patterns differ. The feminine singular is on the pattern تَفْعِينَ, while the feminine plural is on تَفْعَلْنَ.

f: What is the imperative of the defective verb غَزَا → يَغْزُو?
b: The imperative forms are اِغْزُ، اِغْزُوَا، اِغْزُوا، اِغْزِي، اِغْزُوَا، اِغْزُونَ according to the forms listed in the passage.

f: What is the imperative of the defective verb رَمَى → يَرْمِي?
b: The imperative forms are اِرْمِ، اِرْمِيَا، اِرْمُوا، اِرْمِي، اِرْمِيَا، اِرْمِينَ.

f: What is the imperative of the defective verb رَضِيَ → يَرْضَى?
b: The imperative forms are اِرْضَ، اِرْضِيَا، اِرْضُوا، اِرْضِي، اِرْضِيَا، اِرْضِينَ.

f: What happens to the deleted final radical of a defective verb when nūn al-tawkīd (نون التأكيد) is attached?
b: The deleted final radical is restored before nūn al-tawkīd. Thus the source gives forms such as اِغْزُونَّ، اِرْمِيَنَّ، اِرْضَيَنَّ.

f: How is the active participle (اسم الفاعل) formed from a defective verb (الناقص)?
b: Examples include غَازٍ، غَازِيَانِ، غَازُونَ for the masculine, and غَازِيَةٌ، غَازِيَتَانِ، غَازِيَاتٌ for the feminine. Likewise, the active participles of رَمَى and رَضِيَ are رَامٍ and رَاضٍ.

f: What is the original form of the active participle غَازٍ from غَزَا?
b: Its original form is غَازِوٌ. The final wāw is changed into yāʾ because it is final (متطرفة) and the preceding letter has kasrah, just as the wāw is changed in غُزِيَ.

f: Why does the feminine active participle of a defective verb retain the final yāʾ, as in غَازِيَةٌ?
b: The feminine form is treated as a derivative of the masculine, while the tāʾ of femininity is an additional/secondary letter. Thus the yāʾ remains in غَازِيَةٌ.

f: What is the passive participle (اسم المفعول) of a defective wāw-final verb?
b: It is formed with the final weak letter represented as wāw, as in غَزَا → مَغْزُوٌّ.

f: What is the passive participle of a defective yāʾ-final verb?
b: It is formed with the final weak letter as yāʾ, as in رَمَى → مَرْمِيٌّ.

f: Why does the wāw change into yāʾ in the passive participle مَرْمِيٌّ?
b: When wāw and yāʾ occur together in one word and the first of them is sākin, the wāw changes into yāʾ, and the two yāʾs are then assimilated (idghām) into one another.

f: What are examples of the pattern فَعِيل from defective verbs?
b: From a wāw-final verb: صَبِيٌّ; from a yāʾ-final verb: شَقِيٌّ.

f: What happens to a wāw in an augmented defective verb when it occurs as the fourth radical or later?
b: A wāw occurring in the fourth position or beyond is changed into yāʾ if the preceding letter is not ḍammah. Thus: أَعْطَى → يُعْطِي، اعْتَدَى → يَعْتَدِي، اسْتَرْشَى → يَسْتَرْشِي.

f: What happens to the final weak letter of augmented defective verbs when they are connected to a pronoun?
b: The weak letter remains as yāʾ in forms such as أَعْطَيْتُ، اعْتَدَيْتُ، اسْتَرْشَيْتُ. The same applies to forms such as تَغَازَيْنَا and تَرَاجَيْنَا.

f: What is al-lafīf al-maqrūn (اللفيف المقرون)?
b: It is a verb in which the middle and final radicals are both weak. Thus it is called al-muʿtall al-ʿayn wa-l-lām (المعتل العين واللام).

f: What are examples of al-lafīf al-maqrūn?
b: Examples include شَوَى → يَشْوِي، قَوِيَ → يَقْوَى، رَوِيَ → يَرْوَى، حَيِيَ → يَحْيَا.

f: How does شَوَى → يَشْوِي behave morphologically?
b: It follows the general treatment of a defective verb with two adjacent weak radicals, with the relevant changes occurring in its conjugation. Its verbal noun is شَيًّا.

f: What are the forms of قَوِيَ and its verbal noun?
b: قَوِيَ → يَقْوَى → قُوَّةً.

f: What are the active participle forms of رَوِيَ?
b: The masculine active participle is رَيَّانٌ, and the feminine is رَيَّا. They follow the pattern of عَطْشَانٌ

f: What is the augmented form of رَوِيَ, and what verb does it correspond to?
b: أَرْوَى corresponds to أَعْطَى in its morphological treatment.

f: How does حَيِيَ conjugate in the past and present?
b: حَيِيَ → يَحْيَا → حَيَاةً. Its active participle is حَيٌّ, and its forms include حَيَا، حَيِيَا.

f: What are the dual and plural forms of حَيٌّ?
b: The dual is حَيَّانِ, while the plural is أَحْيَاءُ.

f: What alternative form is permitted for the plural of حَيِيَ?
b: حَيُوا may also be used with lightening (التخفيف), analogous to رَضُوا.

f: What is the imperative of حَيِيَ → يَحْيَا?
b: The imperative is اِحْيَ (or أَحْيِ in the corresponding augmented form), following the treatment of اِرْضَ.

f: How does the augmented verb أَحْيَا conjugate?
b: أَحْيَا → يُحْيِي, following the same pattern as أَعْطَى → يُعْطِي.

f: How does the reciprocal form of حَيِيَ behave?
b: The form حَايَا → يُحَايِي → مُحَايَاةً follows the corresponding augmented morphological pattern.

f: How does اسْتَحْيَا conjugate?
b: اسْتَحْيَا → يَسْتَحْيِي → اسْتِحْيَاءً. Its imperative is اسْتَحْيِ.

f: What shortened form of اسْتَحْيَا is used by some Arabs because of frequent usage?
b: Some Arabs use اسْتَحَى → يَسْتَحِي → اسْتَحِ, with deletion caused by the frequency of usage (لكثرة الاستعمال).

f: What is an example of a verb whose weak letters require special treatment because of frequent usage?
b: The passage gives وَقَى → يَقِي, whose imperative is قِ. Its forms include قِ، قِيَا، قُوا، قِينَ.

f: How is the imperative of وَقَى → يَقِي conjugated?
b: It is قِ، قِيَا، قُوا، قِي، قِيَا، قِينَ according to the corresponding imperative forms.

f: What happens when nūn al-tawkīd is attached to وَقَى → يَقِي?
b: The source gives forms such as قِيَنَّ، قِيَانِّ، قِنَّ. With the light nūn (النون الخفيفة), forms such as قِيَنْ، قِنْ occur.

f: What happens when nūn al-tawkīd is attached to a verb such as وَقَى → يَقِي with the heavy and light forms?
b: With the heavy nūn, forms include قِيَنَّ، قِيَانِّ، قِنَّ; with the light nūn, forms include قِيَنْ، قِنْ.

f: How does وَجِيَ → يُوجَى behave?
b: It follows the pattern of رَضِيَ → يَرْضَى, with the corresponding weak-letter changes.

f: What is the imperative of وَجِيَ → يُوجَى?
b: Its imperative is إِيجَ (analogous to اِرْضَ).

f: What is al-lafīf al-mafrūq (اللفيف المفروق)?
b: It is the type of weak verb in which the first and final radicals are weak, while the middle radical is sound. The passage begins its discussion with an example such as وَقَى and then proceeds to the sixth category, المعتل الفاء والعين.

f: What is the sixth type of weak verb mentioned in the passage?
b: The sixth type is al-muʿtall al-fāʾ wa-l-ʿayn (المعتل الفاء والعين), meaning that both the first and middle radicals are weak. The passage gives يَيْن as an example in discussing the noun of place.

f: What is the rule governing a hamzated verb (المهموز) in its conjugation?
b: The rule governing a hamzated verb is the same as that of a sound verb (الصحيح), because the hamzah is a sound consonant (حرف صحيح). However, the hamzah may undergo takhfīf (خفّة) when it occurs anywhere other than the beginning.

f: Why may the hamzah be lightened (تخفيف الهمزة)?
b: The hamzah may be lightened because it is a شدّة consonant articulated from the deepest part of the throat (أقصى الحلق).

f: How is أَمَلَ conjugated in the present tense?
b: أَمَلَ يَأْمَلُ, like نَصَرَ يَنْصُرُ.

f: What is the imperative of أَمَلَ يَأْمَلُ?
b: The imperative is أَوْمَلْ, with the second hamzah changed into a wāw.

f: Why is the second hamzah of أَوْمَلْ changed into a wāw?
b: When two hamzahs occur together in one word and the second is sākin, the second hamzah is changed according to the vowel before it. This is analogous to آمَنَ، أُومِنُ، إِيمَانٌ.

f: What happens to the second hamzah when two hamzahs meet and the first is a hamzat waṣl?
b: The second hamzah returns to being a hamzah in connected speech (الوصل) when the letter before it has fatḥah.

f: Which imperatives have the hamzah deleted irregularly because of frequent usage?
b: The imperatives خُذْ، كُلْ، مُرْ have the hamzah deleted contrary to the regular pattern because of their frequent usage.

f: Can مُرْ ever retain the hamzah?
b: Yes. مُرْ may occur according to the original form when connected to what follows, as in the Qur'anic expression: وَأْمُرْ أَهْلَكَ بِالصَّلَاةِ.

f: How is أَزَرَ conjugated?
b: أَزَرَ يَأْزِرُ, like ضَرَبَ يَضْرِبُ. Its imperative is إِيزِرْ.

f: How is هَنَّأَ
b: هَنِئَ يَهْنَأُ

ar.b: يَهْنِئُ according to the transmitted form; it is treated according to the patterns of the sound verb.

f: How is أَدُبَ conjugated?
b: أَدُبَ يَأْدُبُ, like كَرُمَ يَكْرُمُ. Its imperative is أَوْدُبْ.

f: How is سَأَلَ conjugated?
b: سَأَلَ يَسْأَلُ, like مَنَعَ يَمْنَعُ. Its imperative is إِسْأَلْ.

f: What alternative forms are mentioned for the imperative of سَأَلَ?
b: The forms سَلْ and سَاءَلْ are mentioned in the transmitted discussion; the common irregular imperative is سَلْ.

f: How is آبَ conjugated?
b: آبَ يَؤُوبُ, like صَانَ يَصُونُ.

f: How is سَاءَ conjugated?
b: سَاءَ يَسُوءُ, like صَانَ يَصُونُ.

f: How is جَاءَ conjugated?
b: جَاءَ يَجِيءُ, like كَالَ يَكِيلُ. Its active participle is جَائٍ

f: What are the active participles of سَاءَ and جَاءَ?
b: The passage gives سَاءٍ and جَاءٍ.

f: How is أَسَا conjugated?
b: أَسَا يَأْسُو, like دَعَا يَدْعُو.

f: How is أَتَى conjugated?
b: أَتَى يَأْتِي, like رَمَى يَرْمِي. Its imperative is إِيتِ.

f: What alternative imperative of أَتَى is mentioned?
b: Some Arabs say تِ by analogy with خُذْ, treating it as a shortened irregular imperative.

f: How is وَأَى conjugated?
b: وَأَى يَئِي, according to the pattern given in the passage, analogous to وَقَى يَقِي.

f: How is أَوَى conjugated?
b: أَوَى يَأْوِي.

f: What is unusual about رَأَى in the present tense?
b: Although its regular pattern would give يَرْأَى, the Arabs unanimously deleted the hamzah from its present tense and use يَرَى instead.

f: How is رَأَى conjugated in the third-person masculine singular and dual?
b: يَرَى، يَرَيَانِ.

f: How is رَأَى conjugated in the third-person masculine plural?
b: يَرَوْنَ.

f: How is رَأَى conjugated in the second-person masculine singular and dual?
b: تَرَى، تَرَيَانِ.

f: How is رَأَى conjugated in the second-person masculine plural?
b: تَرَوْنَ.

f: How is رَأَى conjugated in the second-person feminine singular and plural?
b: تَرَيْنَ is used for both, although the underlying morphological patterns differ: the singular is on تَفْعِينَ, while the plural is on تَفْعَلْنَ.

f: How is رَأَى conjugated in the first-person singular and plural?
b: أَرَى، نَرَى.

f: What is unusual about the second-person feminine forms of رَأَى?
b: The second-person feminine singular and plural are identical in pronunciation: تَرَيْنَ. Their underlying morphological weights, however, are different.

f: What is the regular imperative of رَأَى?
b: According to the original pattern, it would be اِرْأَ.

f: What shortened imperative of رَأَى is used after deleting the hamzah?
b: The shortened imperative is رَ.

f: What happens to the final hāʾ when the shortened imperative رَ is paused upon?
b: The hāʾ is retained in pause: رَهْ، رَيَا، رَوْا، رِي، رَيَا، رَيْنَ according to the forms transmitted in the passage.

f: How is the imperative of رَأَى formed with emphatic nūn (نون التوكيد)?
b: The forms given include رَيَنَّ، رَيَانِّ، رَوُنَّ and their corresponding forms according to the conjugation.

f: What are the active participle forms of رَأَى?
b: رَاءٍ، رَائِيَانِ، رَاؤُونَ, analogous to رَاعٍ، رَاعِيَانِ، رَاعُونَ.

f: What is the passive participle of رَأَى?
b: The passive participle is مَرْئِيّ, analogous to مَرْعِيّ.

f: How does the Form IV verb أَرَى differ from the other hamzated verbs discussed?
b: Its conjugation and derivation are exceptional in several forms. It is conjugated أَرَى يُرِي إِرَاءَةً, with the alternative verbal nouns إِرَاء and إِرَايَة also transmitted.

f: What is the active participle of أَرَى?
b: It is مُرٍ

f: What are the feminine active-participle forms of أَرَى?
b: The passage gives مُرِيَّة، مُرِيَّتَانِ، مُرِيَّات.

f: What is the passive participle of أَرَى?
b: The passive participle is given as مُرًى

f: What is the imperative of أَرَى?
b: The imperative forms are أَرِ، أَرِيَا، أَرَوْا، أَرِي، أَرِيَا، أَرَيْنَ.

f: What are the emphatic forms of the imperative of أَرَى?
b: The passage gives forms such as أَرِينَ، أَرِيَانِ، أَرِنَّ and their corresponding feminine forms.

f: How is the negative command (النهي) of أَرَى formed?
b: It is formed with لا followed by the jussive: لَا تُرِ، لَا تُرِيَا، لَا تُرَوْا، لَا تُرِي، لَا تُرِيَا، لَا تُرَيْنَ.

f: How is the negative command of أَرَى formed with nūn al-tawkīd?
b: The passage gives emphatic forms such as لَا تَرَيَنَّ، لَا تَرِيَانِّ، لَا تَرَوُنَّ and their corresponding forms.

f: What is the general rule for the place noun (اسم المكان) derived from a triliteral verb?
b: When derived from a triliteral verb, the place noun is generally formed on مَفْعِل when the present tense has a kasrah on the ʿayn, and on مَفْعَل in the relevant cases where the ʿayn is fatḥah.

f: What pattern does the place noun follow when the present tense has a kasrah on its ʿayn?
b: It generally follows مَفْعِل, such as مَجْلِس from يَجْلِسُ.

f: What pattern does the place noun follow when the present tense has a fatḥah on its ʿayn?
b: It generally follows مَفْعَل, such as مَذْهَب، مَقْتَل، مَشْرَب، مَسْقَط، مَرْفَق، مَفْرَق، مَسْكَن، مَنْسَك.

f: Is fatḥah on the ʿayn of place nouns ever transmitted in forms that normally have kasrah?
b: Yes. Fatḥah is transmitted for some of them, and some grammarians permit fatḥah throughout these forms.

f: What condition is mentioned for the general place-noun rule?
b: The general rule applies when the verb is sound in both its initial radical (الفاء) and final radical (اللام).

f: What happens with a defective-initial verb (معتل الفاء) when forming the place noun?
b: The ʿayn of the place noun is always given kasrah, as in مَوْضِع and مَوْعِد.

f: What happens with a defective-final verb (معتل اللام) when forming the place noun?
b: The ʿayn is always given fatḥah, as in مَأْوَى and مَرْمَى.

f: Can some place nouns take the feminine tāʾ (تاء التأنيث)?
b: Yes. Examples include مَظِنَّة، مَقْبَرَة، مَشْرَقَة.

f: Which place nouns are reported with ḍammah as an exceptional form?
b: مَقْبُرَة and مَشْرُقَة are reported exceptionally with ḍammah.

f: How are place nouns derived from verbs exceeding three radicals?
b: For verbs exceeding three radicals, the place noun follows the pattern of the passive participle (اسم المفعول), such as مُدْخَل.

f: What is the definition of the instrument noun (اسم الآلة)?
b: اسم الآلة is a noun denoting something by which the agent acts upon the object, allowing the effect of the action to reach it.

f: What are the principal patterns of the instrument noun (اسم الآلة)?
b: It occurs on patterns such as مِفْعَل، مِفْعَلة، مِفْعال، مِفْعَاة, exemplified by مِخْلَب، مِكْسَحَة، مِفْتَاح، مِصْفَاة.

f: What exceptional form of an instrument noun is mentioned?
b: مِرْقَاة is reported with kasrah on the mīm.

f: What does فتح الميم in مَرْقَاة indicate according to the passage?
b: If the mīm is given fatḥah, the intended meaning is place (المكان) rather than an instrument.

f: How is the noun indicating a single occurrence (اسم المرة) formed from a basic triliteral verb (الثلاثي المجرد)?
b: It is formed from the verbal noun (المصدر) of the basic triliteral verb on the pattern فَعْلَة, with fatḥah on the first radical.

f: What are examples of the noun indicating a single occurrence (اسم المرة) from a basic triliteral verb?
b: From ضَرَبَ: ضَرْبَة (“one strike”); from قَامَ: قَوْمَة (“one act of standing”).

f: How is the noun indicating a single occurrence formed from a verb with more than three radicals?
b: It is formed by adding تاء التأنيث to the verbal noun, such as إِعْطَاءَة and انْطِلَاقَة.

f: What exception applies when forming اسم المرة from a verbal noun that already contains تاء التأنيث?
b: If the verbal noun already contains تاء التأنيث, another tāʾ is not added. Instead, the occurrence of the action is specified by using واحدة (“one”).

f: How is a single occurrence expressed when the verbal noun already ends in تاء التأنيث?
b: One says, for example, رَحِمْتُهُ رَحْمَةً وَاحِدَةً (“I showed him mercy once”) and دَحْرَجْتُهُ دَحْرَجَةً وَاحِدَةً (“I rolled it once”).

f: How is the noun indicating a manner or type of an action (اسم الهيئة) formed?
b: For the basic triliteral verb, اسم الهيئة is formed on the pattern فِعْلَة, with kasrah on the first radical.

f: What does اسم الهيئة indicate?
b: اسم الهيئة indicates the manner, form, or particular way in which an action is performed, rather than merely one occurrence of the action.

f: What is the difference between فَعْلَة as اسم المرة and فِعْلَة as اسم الهيئة?
b: فَعْلَة with fatḥah indicates one occurrence of the action, whereas فِعْلَة with kasrah indicates the manner or form in which the action is performed.

f: Who wrote the commentary on the Mukhtaṣar al-Taṣrīf discussed in this passage?
b: The commentary was written by Saʿd al-Dīn Masʿūd ibn ʿUmar al-Taftāzānī رحمه الله (مسعود بن عمر القاضي التفتازاني).

f: Which work by al-Zanjānī is being commented upon?
b: It is the Mukhtaṣar al-Taṣrīf (مختصر التصريف), authored by Imām ʿIzz al-Millah wa-l-Dīn al-Zanjānī (الزنجاني).

f: How does al-Taftāzānī رحمه الله describe al-Zanjānī and his Mukhtaṣar al-Taṣrīf?
b: He describes al-Zanjānī as an eminent scholar and exemplar of the verifying scholars, and describes the Mukhtaṣar as a concise work containing noble discussions and subtle principles.

f: Why did al-Taftāzānī رحمه الله decide to write a commentary on the Mukhtaṣar al-Taṣrīf?
b: He wished to explain it in a way that makes its difficult wording easy, unveils the meanings concealed behind its expressions, clarifies its subtle points, and extracts its deeper insights, while adding valuable benefits and useful additions.

f: What does al-Taftāzānī رحمه الله hope readers will do if they find an error in his commentary?
b: He asks readers who encounter an error to repel the evil with good—that is, to respond graciously and overlook his mistake.

f: What does al-Taftāzānī رحمه الله say about the nature of his commentary?
b: He says it is the first work he has arranged and organized in this form, and that he has condensed into this Mukhtaṣar what he studied in the science of ṣarf.

f: Upon whom does al-Taftāzānī رحمه الله rely for assistance in his work?
b: He seeks assistance from Allah, and says that to Him is the means of drawing near; He is sufficient for whoever relies upon Him.

f: Why should a student first form a conception of the subject he wishes to study?
b: A student should first conceive the thing being sought so that he may have insight and clarity in pursuing it.

f: Why should a student know the goal of the science he is studying?
b: Knowing its goal provides the motive and reason that drives him to begin studying it.

f: What does al-Zanjānī begin with in the Mukhtaṣar al-Taṣrīf?
b: He begins by defining taṣrīf, in a manner that also indicates its benefit, while mentioning its linguistic meaning to show the relationship between its linguistic and technical meanings.

f: What is the linguistic meaning of taṣrīf (التصريف)?
b: Taṣrīf linguistically means change (التغيير).

f: What is the technical definition of taṣrīf according to al-Zanjānī?
b: In technical usage, taṣrīf is تحويل الأصل الواحد إلى أمثلة مختلفة لمعانٍ مقصودة لا تحصل إلا بها: transforming one original form into different forms for intended meanings that cannot be obtained except through those forms.

f: What does the word تصريف grammatically indicate?
b: تصريف is the verbal noun (تفعيل) of صَرَفَ, with the pattern of taflīl conveying intensification and multiplication.

f: What are the two meanings of taṣrīf discussed by al-Taftāzānī رحمه الله?
b: It has a linguistic meaning (لغوي), namely change, and a technical/scientific meaning (صناعي), namely transforming one original form into different forms for different intended meanings.

f: What is the linguistic meaning of taṣrīf according to the Arabs' language?
b: Its linguistic meaning is التغيير, “change.” One says صَرَفْتُ الشيءَ, meaning “I changed the thing.”

f: What does “language” (اللغة) mean in the explanation of taṣrīf?
b: Language consists of expressions established for meanings: الألفاظ الموضوعة للمعاني.

f: What is the etymological discussion of the word لغة given by al-Taftāzānī رحمه الله?
b: He relates it to لَغِيَ

f: What does “in the technical discipline” (وفي الصناعة) mean in the definition of taṣrīf?
b: It means the meaning assigned to taṣrīf by the specialists of this discipline—namely, the technical science of ṣarf.

f: What does the term صناعة mean in this context?
b: Ṣināʿah here means a science or skill acquired through practicing an activity; here it means the discipline of ṣarf.

f: What is the technical meaning of taṣrīf in ṣarf?
b: It is transforming one original form into different patterns and forms for intended meanings.

f: What does “the one original” (الأصل الواحد) mean in the definition of taṣrīf?
b: The “one original” means the thing upon which something else is built; here it refers specifically to the maṣdar (verbal noun).

f: What does “into different examples” (إلى أمثلة مختلفة) mean in the definition of taṣrīf?
b: It means transforming the original into different patterns, structures, and forms (أبنية وصيغ).

f: What are “forms” (أبنية وصيغ) in the science of ṣarf?
b: They are words considered according to the forms imposed upon them, such as their vowels, sukūns, and the ordering or rearrangement of their letters.

f: What does it mean that the patterns are “different” (مختلفة)?
b: They differ because their structural features differ, such as ضَرَبَ and يَضْرِبُ, along with other derived forms.

f: What does “meanings” (معانٍ) refer to in the definition of taṣrīf?
b: It refers to the meanings intended by the different forms of the word.

f: What is the original meaning of مَعْنًى according to al-Taftāzānī رحمه الله?
b: مَعْنًى is originally discussed as a verbal noun of ʿināyah (العناية) that was transferred to mean the object intended by an expression—that is, what is meant by the wording.

f: Why does taṣrīf transform one original form into different patterns?
b: It does so to obtain intended meanings that cannot be obtained except through those different forms.

f: What example demonstrates the practical need for the science of taṣrīf?
b: Ḍarb (الضرب) is the original meaning/form. Transforming it into ضَرَبَ، يَضْرِبُ, and other forms allows one to express whether the act of striking occurred in the past, present, or another grammatical circumstance.

f: What does the definition of taṣrīf demonstrate about the usefulness of ṣarf?
b: It demonstrates that ṣarf is necessary because changing the form of an original word allows different intended meanings to be expressed.

f: What kind of “taṣrīf” is being defined in this passage?
b: The passage is defining taṣrīf as a process of transforming words, not the separate science called ʿilm al-taṣrīf, which is the knowledge of the states and forms of word patterns.

f: Why did al-Zanjānī use the word “transformation” (تحويل) rather than simply “change” (تغيير)?
b: He chose تحويل because it contains the additional sense of transferring something from one state or place to another.

f: How does al-Maghrib define التحويل?
b: It defines التحويل as نقل الشيء من موضع إلى آخر—transferring a thing from one place to another.

f: How does al-Ṣiḥāḥ define التحويل?
b: It defines it as التنقل من موضع إلى موضع آخر—moving or transferring from one place to another.

f: What Qur'anic expression is cited in the explanation of التحويل?
b: The verse لَا يَبْغُونَ عَنْهَا حِوَلًا is cited, illustrating the semantic connection of ḥawl/ḥiwal with changing or moving from one state or place.

f: Why is التحويل more specific than التغيير?
b: Taḥwīl involves transferring something from one position or state to another, whereas taghyīr is broader and simply means change.

f: Why is transforming the letters of ضَرْب into ضَرَبَ and يَضْرِبُ appropriately described as تحويل?
b: Because the letters and structure of the original are transferred into different configurations and forms, such as ضَرَبَ and يَضْرِبُ.

f: Why can taṣrīf not be defined linguistically as التحويل?
b: Because taḥwīl is more specific than taṣrīf. Therefore, defining the broader linguistic meaning of taṣrīf as the narrower term taḥwīl would not be correct.

f: What four types of causes (العلل الأربع) does the definition of taṣrīf contain?
b: The definition contains the material cause (العلة المادية), formal cause (العلة الصورية), efficient/agent cause (العلة الفاعلية), and final/purpose cause (العلة الغائية).

f: What is the material cause (العلة المادية) indicated in the definition of taṣrīf?
b: The original upon which the transformation is based (الأصل الواحد), namely the verbal noun (المصدر), represents the material basis.

f: What is the formal cause (العلة الصورية) indicated in the definition of taṣrīf?
b: The different patterns and forms (الأمثلة المختلفة

f: What is the final cause (العلة الغائية) indicated in the definition of taṣrīf?
b: The intended meanings (المعاني المقصودة) that are obtained through the different forms constitute the final cause.

f: What is the efficient cause (العلة الفاعلية) in the definition of taṣrīf?
b: The agent performing the transformation, namely the speaker or one who applies the rules of ṣarf, constitutes the efficient cause.

f: Which part of the definition of taṣrīf represents the formal cause (العلة الصورية)?
b: التحويل (transformation) represents the formal cause.

f: How does the definition of taṣrīf indicate the efficient cause (العلة الفاعلية)?
b: It indicates it by implication through the one who performs the transformation (المحوِّل).

f: Which part of the definition of taṣrīf represents the material cause (العلة المادية)?
b: الأصل الواحد (the one original) represents the material cause.

f: Which part of the definition of taṣrīf represents the final cause (العلة الغائية)?
b: حصول المعاني المقصودة (the attainment of the intended meanings) represents the final cause.

f: Who is the “transformer” (المحوِّل) in the definition of taṣrīf?
b: In ordinary usage, it can refer to anyone capable of performing the transformation, as when one says صَرَفْتُ الكلمة (“I transformed the word”). More precisely, however, the transformer is the واضع (the one who established the language).

f: Why is the واضع considered the true transformer in ṣarf?
b: Because he is the one who originally transformed the single original into its various patterns and forms.

f: What does it mean to say that the واضع “transformed the one original into the examples”?
b: It means that he derived the various forms from the one original, rather than establishing every individual form as an entirely independent linguistic pattern.

f: Why is it preferable to regard the various forms as derived from one original rather than as independently established forms?
b: This approach has a stronger correspondence between the forms and their common origin and makes the system easier to regulate and memorize.

f: Why did al-Zanjānī choose the expression “the one original” (الأصل الواحد) instead of simply saying “the verbal noun” (المصدر)?
b: He chose الأصل الواحد so that the definition would be valid according to both major theories concerning the origin of derivation.

f: What is the Kūfan position concerning the relationship between the maṣdar and the verb?
b: The Kūfans hold that the maṣdar is derived from the verb, making the verb the original from which the maṣdar is derived.

f: What is the primary evidence used by the Kūfans to argue that the maṣdar is derived from the verb?
b: They argue that the maṣdar undergoes vowel/weak-letter changes (إعلال) according to the changes occurring in the verb, which they take as evidence that the maṣdar is secondary to the verb.

f: How is the Kūfan argument concerning the derivational priority of the verb answered?
b: It is answered that being secondary to something with respect to iʿlāl does not necessarily mean being secondary to it with respect to ishtiqāq (derivation).

f: What example demonstrates that a form can be secondary in iʿlāl without being derived from another form?
b: Forms such as أَعِدْ، نَعِدُ، تَعِدُ are secondary to يَعِدُ with respect to iʿlāl, even though they are not derived from يَعِدُ.

f: Why does the fact that the verb undergoes iʿlāl before the maṣdar contradict neither theory of derivation?
b: Because the order in which forms undergo iʿlāl does not establish their order of derivation. Thus, the verb may undergo iʿlāl before the maṣdar even if the verb itself is considered derivative of the maṣdar.

f: What four causes does Tadrīj al-Adānī identify in ṣarf?
b: Since ṣarf is an intentional process produced by an agent, it contains four causes: material (مادية), formal (صورية), efficient (فاعلية), and final (غائية).

f: Why are the four causes applicable to ṣarf?
b: Because ṣarf is a structured process produced by a deliberate agent, and everything of this kind requires these four explanatory causes.

f: How are the four causes classified generally?
b: A cause is either internal to the effect (داخلة في المعلول) or external to it. An internal cause is either actual in producing the effect or potential: the former is the formal cause, and the latter the material cause. An external cause is either an influence producing the effect—the efficient cause—or something for whose sake the effect occurs—the final cause.

f: What constitutes the material cause in the ṣarf examples?
b: The original letters (حروف الأصل) constitute the material cause.

f: What constitutes the formal cause in the ṣarf examples?
b: The form or configuration (الصورة) resulting from the combination of the original letters and the characteristics imposed upon them constitutes the formal cause.

f: What constitutes the efficient cause in the ṣarf examples?
b: The واضع, the one who established the linguistic forms, constitutes the efficient cause.

f: What constitutes the final cause in the ṣarf examples?
b: The attainment of the intended meanings (حصول المعاني المقصودة) constitutes the final cause.

f: What does the four-cause analysis show about al-Zanjānī's definition of taṣrīf?
b: It shows that the definition implicitly indicates all four causes, which makes the definition particularly comprehensive and well-constructed.

f: What does al-Taftāzānī رحمه الله mean by “maṣdar” when explaining the original in taṣrīf?
b: He means specifically the basic/ungmented maṣdar (المصدر المجرد).

f: Why is the augmented maṣdar (المصدر المزيد فيه) not intended by the term “maṣdar” here?
b: Because the augmented maṣdar is itself derived from the basic maṣdar, sharing its letters and meaning in addition to the augmentation.

f: How can the objection be answered that some ṣarf forms appear to be derived directly from verbs?
b: Although forms such as the imperative, active participle, and passive participle appear to be derived from the verb, ultimately they all trace back to the maṣdar.

f: How are the imperative, active participle, and passive participle related to the maṣdar?
b: They are all ultimately derived from the maṣdar, either directly or through an intermediary (بواسطة أو بلا واسطة).

f: Why might “the one original” (الأصل الواحد) be preferable to “the maṣdar” in the definition of taṣrīf?
b: Because الأصل الواحد is broader than the maṣdar and can include transformations involving nouns as well as verbs.

f: What non-verbal transformations can be included by the expression “the one original”?
b: It can include transforming a noun into the dual (المثنى), plural (المجموع), diminutive (المصغر), nisbah adjective (المنسوب), and similar forms.

f: Which expression does al-Taftāzānī رحمه الله ultimately consider more comprehensive: المصدر or الأصل الواحد?
b: He considers الأصل الواحد more comprehensive and says that this interpretation is closer to what is intended.

f: Why was the term التصريف chosen instead of الصرف?
b: Although التصريف and الصرف share the same basic meaning, التصريف was chosen because this science involves many transformations (تصرفات كثيرة).

f: What does the pattern تفعيل in التصريف contribute to its meaning?
b: The pattern تفعيل conveys intensification and multiplicity (المبالغة والتكثير), making it appropriate for a science involving numerous transformations.

f: What are the three fundamental categories of words in Arabic?
b: Arabic words are divided into three categories: noun (اسم), verb (فعل), and particle (حرف).

f: Why does al-Taftāzānī رحمه الله begin the next discussion with the verb?
b: Because the subject under discussion is the verb and the forms derived from it, so he proceeds to explain the divisions of the verb.

f: How is the word فِعْل distinguished from فَعْل in the passage?
b: فِعْل with kasrah on the fāʾ is the technical noun referring to a particular type of word, whereas فَعَلَ

f: Into how many primary categories is the Arabic verb divided according to the number of its original letters?
b: It is divided into triliteral (ثلاثي) and quadriliteral (رباعي) verbs.

f: Why is the verb divided into triliteral and quadriliteral?
b: Because its original/root letters are either three or four. A verb whose original letters are three is triliteral, while one whose original letters are four is quadriliteral.

f: Why are there no basic Arabic verbs with five or two original letters?
b: Observation and linguistic induction show that Arabic does not construct basic verbs with five or two original letters. The five-letter verb would be excessively heavy, while the two-letter verb would be too weak to accept the various changes that occur in verbs.

f: Why can Arabic nouns have five original letters even though basic verbs do not?
b: The five-letter noun is permitted so that the rank of the verb is not diminished relative to the noun, since the verb is heavier than the noun because it indicates an event, time, and an agent.

f: Why is the division of “every verb into triliteral or quadriliteral” not a circular division?
b: Because the term verb (الفعل) being divided refers to the general concept of a verb without considering whether it has three or four letters. The divisions are therefore subdivisions of the general concept rather than a division of one category into itself and something else.

f: What exactly is the subject of the division into triliteral and quadriliteral?
b: The subject is the concept of “verb” (مفهوم الفعل), not an individual thing to which the concept of verb happens to apply.

f: What is the difference between the concept of “verb” and something to which the concept of “verb” applies?
b: The concept (مفهوم) is the abstract meaning of “verb,” whereas what the concept applies to (ما صدق عليه المفهوم) consists of actual verbs such as individual triliteral and quadriliteral verbs.

f: Into what two categories is each triliteral and quadriliteral verb further divided?
b: Each is either basic/unaugmented (مجرد) or augmented (مزيد فيه).

f: What is a basic/unaugmented verb (مجرد)?
b: A مجرد verb is one whose original/root letters remain without additional letters being added to the pattern.

f: What is an augmented verb (مزيد فيه)?
b: A مزيد فيه verb is one in which letters have been added to its original/root letters.

f: Into what two categories is each of the four types—triliteral basic, triliteral augmented, quadriliteral basic, and quadriliteral augmented—divided?
b: Each is either sound (سالم) or non-sound/defective (غير سالم).

f: What makes a verb sound (سالم) according to this classification?
b: Its original letters must be free from weak letters (حروف العلة), hamzah (الهمزة), and doubling (التضعيف).

f: What makes a verb non-sound (غير سالم)?
b: If its original letters contain a weak letter, hamzah, or a doubled radical, it is classified as non-sound in this terminology.

f: How many major categories result from combining the triliteral/quadriliteral, basic/augmented, and sound/non-sound divisions?
b: The classification produces eight categories.

f: What are examples of the eight categories in the passage?
b: The examples are نَصَرَ، وَعَدَ، أَكْرَمَ، أَوْعَدَ، دَحْرَجَ، زَلْزَلَ، تَدَحْرَجَ، تَزَلْزَلَ.

f: What does “sound” (السالم) mean in the terminology of the ṣarf scholars?
b: In the science of ṣarf, a sound word (السالم) is one whose original radicals corresponding to fāʾ, ʿayn, and lām are free from weak letters (حروف العلة: واو، ألف، ياء), hamzah (الهمزة), and doubling (التضعيف).

f: Why does the definition of السالم specify “original letters” (الحروف الأصلية)?
b: It excludes forms such as مَسَّتْ and ظَلَّتْ, where one of the two doubled letters has been deleted. Such forms are still non-sound because their original forms contain doubling.

f: Why are forms such as قُلْ and بِعْ still classified as non-sound?
b: Because they originate from قُلْتُ / قُلْنَ and بِعْتُ

f: Why are forms such as أَكْرَمَ، اعْشَوْشَبَ، and احْمَارَّ classified as sound?
b: They are sound because their original radicals contain none of the features that define a non-sound verb: no weak radical, hamzah, or original doubling.

f: Can a word still be classified as sound if one of its sound letters has been replaced by a weak letter?
b: Yes. A word may remain classified as sound if one of its sound letters has undergone an ibdāl (إبدال) into a weak letter, as discussed in the longer works of ṣarf.

f: Why is the category called “sound” (سالم)?
b: It is called sound because it is free from many of the changes that commonly occur in non-sound words.

f: What does “the letters corresponding to fāʾ, ʿayn, and lām” refer to?
