b: Not necessarily. The author notes that several of them are names independently assigned to particular containers or objects, rather than productive derivatives of verbs in the technical category of اسم الآلة. Therefore calling them “anomalous” is questionable.

f: What does Sībawayh say about nouns such as مُدْهُن and مُكْحُلَة?
b: Sībawayh says that the Arabs did not treat them according to the verbal derivational pattern; rather, they simply established these words as names for particular containers.

f: Which two of the listed forms can genuinely be treated as anomalous instrument nouns?
b: The passage singles out المِنْخَل and المِدَقّ, because these genuinely function as names of instruments used to perform actions.

f: What regular forms of مِدَقّ are transmitted?
b: Both مِدَقّ and مِدَقَّة, with kasrah on the mīm and fatḥah on the ʿayn, are transmitted according to the regular instrument-noun pattern.

f: What new morphological topic begins after the discussion of instrument nouns?
b: The passage begins discussing اسم المرة, the noun indicating that an action occurred once.

f: What is اسم المرة?
b: اسم المرة is a maṣdar used to indicate one occurrence of an action, considered with respect to the action itself rather than a particular type or manner of performing it.

f: How is اسم المرة formed from a basic triliteral verb?
b: It is normally formed on فَعْلَة, with fatḥah on the fāʾ: ضَرَبَ → ضَرْبَة and قَامَ → قَوْمَة in the relevant morphological principle.

f: What does ضَرْبَة mean as a noun of one occurrence?
b: It means one act of striking—that is, one occurrence of the action of striking.

f: What does قَوْمَة mean according to the morphological principle?
b: It denotes one occurrence of standing, formed according to the same pattern for a single occurrence of the action.

f: How does اسم المرة differ from the basic maṣdar?
b: The basic maṣdar can simply confirm or denote the action without adding a numerical specification, whereas اسم المرة adds the meaning of one occurrence of that action.

f: What are the three broad types of maṣdar mentioned in the commentary?
b: The maṣdar can indicate confirmation/emphasis (التأكيد), one occurrence (المرة), or a particular manner/type (النوع).

f: When does a maṣdar function as a maṣdar of emphasis?
b: When it adds no meaning beyond the meaning already contained in the governing verb, as in ضَرَبْتُهُ ضَرْبًا: “I struck him—striking.”

f: When does a maṣdar function as اسم المرة?
b: When it adds the meaning of number, specifically one occurrence, as in ضَرَبْتُهُ ضَرْبَةً: “I struck him once.”

f: When does a maṣdar function as اسم النوع?
b: When it adds the meaning of manner or type, such as a maṣdar indicating a particular way in which the action was performed.

f: What is the relationship between the original maṣdar and the maṣdar of one occurrence or type?
b: The basic maṣdar is the original form, while the maṣdar of one occurrence and the maṣdar of type are treated as derivatives from it.

f: Are there exceptions to the regular فَعْلَة pattern for اسم المرة from a basic triliteral verb?
b: Yes. The passage gives إِتْيَانَة and لِقَاءَة as anomalous forms. According to regular analogy, the forms would be أَتْيَة and لَقْيَة.

f: How is اسم المرة formed from a verb with more than three letters?
b: It is normally formed by adding tāʾ al-taʾnīth (ـة) to the verb's maṣdar. Examples include إِعْطَاءَة from أَعْطَى and انْطِلَاقَة from انْطَلَقَ.

f: What examples illustrate اسم المرة from derived triliteral or quadriliteral verbs?
b: Examples include إِعْطَاءَة = one act of giving, انْطِلَاقَة = one departure, اسْتِخْرَاجَة = one extraction, and دَحْرَجَة with the added tāʾ when used to specify one occurrence.

f: Why is the added tāʾ of اسم المرة sometimes described as هاء?
b: Because the tāʾ of feminine marking is pronounced as hāʾ when pausing, so the ending may be referred to as هاء in the discussion of the written/final form.

f: Does every maṣdar from a verb with more than three letters need the added tāʾ to indicate one occurrence?
b: Not if the maṣdar already contains feminine tāʾ. In that case, simply adding another tāʾ would not adequately distinguish the intended meaning, so the phrase مَرَّةً وَاحِدَةً (“once”) must be added.

f: How is the single occurrence expressed when the maṣdar already ends in feminine tāʾ?
b: The maṣdar is followed by وَاحِدَةً, as in رَحِمْتُهُ رَحْمَةً وَاحِدَةً and دَحْرَجْتُهُ دَحْرَجَةً وَاحِدَةً.

f: Why can a maṣdar already ending in feminine tāʾ not simply receive another tāʾ to form اسم المرة?
b: Because the maṣdar already has the same formal marker. Adding another tāʾ would not provide a clear or normal morphological distinction for the meaning “one occurrence.”

f: Give an example of اسم المرة from a verb whose maṣdar already ends in feminine tāʾ.
b: قَاتَلْتُهُ مُقَاتَلَةً وَاحِدَةً means “I fought him once,” because مُقَاتَلَة already ends in feminine tāʾ.

f: What is the rule for اسم المرة from the basic triliteral verb when its normal maṣdar does not already contain feminine tāʾ?
b: Add the pattern فَعْلَة to indicate one occurrence, such as ضَرْبَة from ضَرَبَ.

f: What is the rule for اسم المرة from a verb of more than three letters whose maṣdar does not already contain feminine tāʾ?
b: Add feminine tāʾ to the maṣdar, such as إِعْطَاءَة and انْطِلَاقَة.

f: What is the rule when the maṣdar of a derived or quadriliteral verb already contains feminine tāʾ?
b: The maṣdar itself is retained and the meaning of one occurrence is expressed by adding وَاحِدَةً, as in رَحْمَةً وَاحِدَةً، دَحْرَجَةً وَاحِدَةً، مُقَاتَلَةً وَاحِدَةً، طُمَأْنِينَةً وَاحِدَةً.

f: Are maṣdars containing feminine tāʾ always formed by productive analogy?
b: No. Some are regularly derived, while others are lexically transmitted (samāʿī) and must simply be learned from usage.

f: Which maṣdars containing feminine tāʾ are described as regularly formed?
b: The passage says the rule applies regularly to the maṣdar of فَعْلَلَ (quadriliteral), فَاعَلَ, certain forms of فَعَلَ with weak final radicals, أَفْعَلَ, and اسْتَفْعَلَ when they are hollow.

f: What is the status of examples such as رَحْمَة, نَشْدَة, and كَدْرَة?
b: These are cited as samāʿī maṣdars containing feminine tāʾ. Their forms cannot simply be generated by analogy; they are established through transmitted Arabic usage.

f: What principle should be followed for maṣdars containing feminine tāʾ when determining whether their form is regular?
b: The regular patterns should be distinguished from lexicalized/samāʿī forms. Where a form is not covered by a productive morphological rule, it should be learned through samaʿ, rather than generated by analogy.

f: What morphological pattern indicates a particular type or manner of an action?
b: For the basic triliteral verb, فَعْلَة with kasrah on the fāʾ (فِعْلَة) indicates a particular type, manner, or state of the action.

f: What is the difference between ضَرْبَة and ضِرْبَة?
b: ضَرْبَة with fatḥah on the fāʾ indicates one occurrence of striking, while ضِرْبَة with kasrah indicates a particular type or manner of striking.

f: What does جَلْسَة mean when used as اسم النوع?
b: جِلْسَة with kasrah on the fāʾ indicates a particular manner or type of sitting.

f: What does اسم النوع mean according to the commentary?
b: It refers to the particular state, manner, or quality in which the agent performs the action. It can describe a characteristic manner that has become associated with the person performing the action.

f: What does حَسَنُ الطِّعْمَة mean in the discussion of اسم النوع?
b: It means that the person has a good manner or quality of eating/tasting, depending on the intended meaning of الطِّعْمَة.

f: What does حَسَنُ الجِلْسَة mean?
b: It means that the person has a good manner of sitting—that is, he sits in a characteristically good or pleasing way.

f: What does حَسَنُ الرَّكْبَة mean as an example of اسم النوع?
b: It means that the person has a good manner of riding, such that this manner has become a characteristic or habitual state of his riding.

f: Why can a particular manner of performing an action be considered a “state” of the agent?
b: Because when a particular manner repeatedly occurs from the agent, it becomes established as a characteristic state or habit associated with him.

f: What do examples such as العَذْرَة، القِتْلَة، and المِيتَة illustrate?
b: They illustrate اسم النوع by referring to the state or manner associated with an event: العَذْرَة is the state in which someone apologizes, القِتْلَة is the manner/state in which someone was killed, and المِيتَة is the state in which someone died or was made to die.

f: Is the distinction between اسم المرة and اسم النوع morphologically visible in every verb?
b: No. The clear morphological distinction between فَعْلَة for one occurrence and فِعْلَة for type applies specifically to the basic triliteral verb whose maṣdar does not already contain feminine tāʾ.

f: How are اسم المرة and اسم النوع distinguished for derived triliteral and quadriliteral verbs?
b: They generally have the same morphological form, so the distinction is determined by external context and accompanying expressions.

f: How would رحمة be distinguished as اسم المرة versus اسم النوع?
b: رَحْمَةً وَاحِدَةً means one occurrence of mercy, i.e. اسم المرة. A contextual description such as رَحْمَةً لَطِيفَةً would indicate a particular type or manner, i.e. اسم النوع.

f: How would دحرجة be distinguished as اسم المرة versus اسم النوع?
b: دَحْرَجْتُهُ دَحْرَجَةً وَاحِدَةً indicates one occurrence. دَحْرَجْتُهُ دَحْرَجَةً لَطِيفَةً or a similar contextual qualification indicates a particular type or manner.

f: How would انطلاقة be distinguished as اسم المرة versus اسم النوع?
b: انْطِلَاقَةً وَاحِدَةً indicates one occurrence, whereas a description such as انْطِلَاقَةً حَسَنَةً or قَبِيحَةً indicates a particular type or manner.

f: What is the general rule for distinguishing اسم المرة and اسم النوع in non-triliteral verbs?
b: They are generally not distinguished by a different morphological pattern. Instead, contextual qualifiers such as “one” distinguish the occurrence, while descriptive qualifiers distinguish the type or manner.

f: What does the phrase “الفرق القرائن الخارجية” mean in the discussion of اسم المرة and اسم النوع?
b: It means that the distinction is made by external contextual indicators, rather than by a difference in the morphological form of the maṣdar itself.

f: If a maṣdar already has feminine tāʾ, how is one occurrence normally expressed?
b: By adding وَاحِدَةً, because the feminine tāʾ is already part of the maṣdar. For example: رَحْمَةً وَاحِدَةً and دَحْرَجَةً وَاحِدَةً.

f: If a maṣdar already has feminine tāʾ, how is a particular type or manner expressed?
b: It is distinguished through an appropriate descriptive or contextual qualifier, such as لَطِيفَةً، حَسَنَةً، قَبِيحَةً and similar expressions.

f: What is the essential distinction between اسم المرة and اسم النوع?
b: اسم المرة answers the question “How many times did the action occur?”, specifically one time; اسم النوع answers “In what manner or type was the action performed?”

f: What does the commentary imply about the source passage after the discussion of اسم النوع?
b: The remaining text is largely scribal/editorial material and colophons recording the completion and copying of the commentary, rather than further substantive discussion of ṣarf.

f: When and by whom does one of the manuscript colophons say the commentary was completed?
b: One colophon states that it was completed by ʿAbd al-Ḥayy al-Kaylānī al-Shāfiʿī al-Ṣīnīnī, with the copying completed on Thursday, the 11th of Jumādā al-Thāniyah, 1308 AH.

f: What do the final manuscript notes primarily contain?
b: They contain scribal colophons, including prayers for forgiveness and blessings upon the Prophet ﷺ, and statements recording the completion of the copying by different scribes.
